author: pixer415
tagline: virt-manager with its own hypervisor, and guest GPU acceleration
description:
**VMM Reloaded** is the full virt-manager interface in your browser, with
a hypervisor of its own, so guests can render on the box's GPU.

- The real virt-manager UI over GTK Broadway - no VNC or RDP client
- Ships its own QEMU built with the OpenGL and virgl modules
- A **GPU Acceleration** window: one switch per machine, no terminal
- Full XML editing, snapshots, storage pools, USB passthrough
- Guest consoles stream in the browser, accelerated or not

**This app brings its own libvirtd.** It does not drive the one behind
ZimaOS's Virtual Machine page, so VMs created here will not show up
there, and VMs created there will not show up here. That separation is
deliberate: it is what lets the app ship a QEMU with GPU support on a
system whose own QEMU may not have it.

**Turning on 3D for a guest.** Create the VM as usual, then switch to the
**GPU Acceleration** window that opens beside Virtual Machine Manager. It
lists every machine with a switch; flick the switch and restart the VM.
**Check GPU** in that window reports on the whole chain - render node,
QEMU modules, Mesa, libvirt - and names any layer that is missing.

Do not use the **OpenGL** checkbox on virt-manager's own Display page. It
selects SPICE's local-only dmabuf path, which a browser cannot display;
the switch sets up the arrangement that does work.

**If you prefer the command line,** the terminal icon at the bottom left
opens a tmux session with `shell` in front and `virt-manager` behind it,
carrying the program's output and any SSH password prompt. `virt-3d list`,
`virt-3d enable <vm>` and `virt-gpu-check` do the same jobs there.

tips.before_install:
**This app runs its own hypervisor.** VMs you create here will not
appear on ZimaOS's Virtual Machine page, and vice versa. Install it as
a replacement for that page, not an addition to it.

**Hardware.** `/dev/kvm` is needed for usable speed and `/dev/dri` for
guest 3D. Both are granted below. The app still starts without them,
with a warning in the log and software rendering.

**Storage.** Guest disks default to
`/DATA/AppData/virt-manager-reloaded/images`, which lives on the system
volume. Point that mount at a larger pool before you build big VMs.

**After installing,** open the tile, create a VM, then use the **GPU
Acceleration** window that opens beside Virtual Machine Manager: one
switch per machine, then restart the machine. No command line needed.
